issues.passage: The report did not presage any future risk; it merely listed last quarter's completed projects.
issues.why: Valid, natural use of presage = be a sign of a future event: the sentence correctly states that the report did not foreshadow future risk and only listed past work.

fix.correctPassage: A sudden drop in overnight temperatures seemed to presage an early frost.
wrongPassages: The historian used new archival letters to presage what had already happened a century earlier.
After the treaty was signed, diplomats gathered to presage the outcome they had just secured.
The archivist carefully presaged each donated letter by date and sender for the collection catalog.
